_comment: Maps the content RetroArch reports (GET_STATUS) to a memory profile key.
GBA ROM headers are useless for this: every hack keeps its base game's
title and code, so Unbound, Gaia and TRE all read 'POKEMON FIRE'/BPRE.
CRC32 of the ROM file is the only exact discriminator, with the reported
content NAME as a fallback for a differently-patched dump.
'strict' entries refuse to match on name alone. Vanilla Emerald must not
claim 'Pokemon Emerald Rogue' just because the word Emerald appears —
reading an unknown hack through a vanilla profile is the exact failure
this file exists to prevent, so an unrecognised CRC stays unrecognised.
'strict' is for VANILLA entries only: every hack keeps its base game's title,
so name-matching would let a hack claim Emerald or FireRed. A hack whose own
token cannot appear in another title does not need it, and marking one strict
means an unrecognised CRC leaves it undetectable — Pisces sat on the previous
game's profile with an empty party and said nothing.
